title: Discovered Attacks
subtitle: Move one piece, unleash another.
goals: Make the moving piece work too

steps.say: A discovered attack is chess's version of a trapdoor: one piece steps aside and a hidden attacker behind it strikes. The magic — the piece that MOVES can create a second threat at the same time. Two threats, one move, and your opponent can only answer one.

steps.prompt: Your knight masks the rook's check. Move it somewhere VICIOUS — discovered check plus a queen attack!
hints: Any knight move uncovers Re1's check — so pick the jump that creates a second threat.
From c6 the knight attacks d8. Check from the rook, queen attacked by the knight — Black can't handle both.

line.say: Discovered check! The rook checks while the knight leaps onto the queen — Black must answer the CHECK first...
...so the queen is simply taken. The discovered check bought you a free capture.

rejections.say: Discovered check, yes — but the knight retreated to do nothing. The whole art is making the MOVING piece threaten something too. Try attacking the queen.

steps.wrongSay: Every knight move gives discovered check — but only one ALSO attacks the queen.
steps.successSay: Discovered check + second threat = your opponent answers the check while you take the prize.

steps.prompt: The knight blocks your bishop's long diagonal to a8. Unleash it — with check!
hints: When the knight moves, the g2 bishop suddenly sees the corner rook. Make the knight move COUNT.
A knight check on e7 forces the king to respond while the bishop's attack hangs over a8.

line.say: Check from the knight — AND the long diagonal opens onto the rook...
The rook is gone. Even when Black rounds up your knight, you've won the exchange — rook for knight.

rejections.say: The knight attacks the rook AND the bishop sees it — but Black just moves the rook, saving everything. The knight CHECK froze Black completely; that's the difference.

steps.wrongSay: Open the bishop's diagonal with a knight move that gives CHECK — no time for Black to save the rook.
steps.successSay: Discoveries with check are 'free moves' — your opponent is busy while you collect.

steps.prompt: DOUBLE CHECK — the rarest, most forcing move in chess. Both pieces check at once; blocking is impossible!
hints: Move the bishop so IT checks the king while the rook behind checks too. Against double check, only a king move is legal — no blocks, no captures.
Bishop to c6: two checks, one move, and the a8 rook is on the bishop's new diagonal.

line.say: DOUBLE CHECK! Rook and bishop check together — Black cannot block two lines and cannot capture two pieces. The king must run...
...and the bishop, still sitting on its checking diagonal, scoops the rook. Total domination.

rejections.say: It attacks the rook and discovers check — good! But Bc6+ was DOUBLE check: king forced to move, rook collected next. When both pieces can check, always prefer it.

steps.wrongSay: Find the bishop move that checks e8 BY ITSELF while the rook checks behind it.
steps.successSay: Double check answers itself: the king must move, whatever else is happening on the board.

steps.prompt: Every knight move discovers check — but the queen on a5 demands a special one. Find the discovery that wins her!
hints: The knight should attack the queen WHILE the rook checks. Which jumps hit a5?
c4 and c6 both touch the queen. Either way, when Black blocks the check with the queen, take her!

line.say: Discovered check plus attack on the queen!
The queen's only try was blocking the check — straight into your rook. Queen won.
Discovered check while the knight lunges at the queen!
Blocking was forced — and fatal. The queen falls with check.

rejections.say: Discovered check — but the knight attacks nothing, so Black simply plays Kd8 and the queen is untouched. Make the knight hit her directly: Nc4 or Nc6, and she's lost whatever Black does.
Greedy — a pawn and a discovered check, but the knight hangs on f7 and the queen escapes the danger. The clean discoveries attack the QUEEN so every reply loses her.

steps.wrongSay: The discovery must do double duty: rook checks, knight attacks the queen. Two squares do it.
steps.successSay: That's mastery: not just finding a discovery, but choosing the one that wins the most.
